The '''Serpentine Galleries''' are two contemporary [[art galleries]] in [[Kensington Gardens]], [[Westminster]], [[Greater London]]. Rebranded as Serpentine in 2022,<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-12|title=London's Serpentine Galleries finally removes Sackler name from building, replacing it with North|url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2022/01/12/serpentine-removes-sackler-name-from-building-replacing-it-with-north|access-date=2022-02-24|website=The Art Newspaper - International art news and events}}</ref> the organisation is split across Serpentine South (previously known as the Serpentine Gallery) and Serpentine North (previously known as the Sackler Gallery). 

The gallery spaces are within five minutes' walk of each other, linked by the bridge over the [[Serpentine Lake]] from which the galleries get their names. Their exhibitions, architecture, education and public programmes attract up to 1.2 million visitors a year. Admission to both galleries is free. The [[Chief executive officer|CEO]] is [[Bettina Korek]], and the artistic director [[Hans Ulrich Obrist]].

==Serpentine South==
Serpentine South, previously known as the Serpentine Gallery, was established in 1970 and is housed in a [[listed building|Grade II listed]] former tea pavilion built in 1933–34 by the architect [[James Grey West]].<ref name=EnglishHeritage01>{{National Heritage List for England |num= 1217605|desc= Serpentine Art Gallery|access-date= 28 September 2014}}</ref> Notable artists whose works have been exhibited there include [[Man Ray]], [[Henry Moore]], [[Jean-Michel Basquiat]], [[Andy Warhol]], [[Paula Rego]], [[Sondra Perry]], [[Bridget Riley]], [[Allan McCollum]],<ref>[[Liam Gillick]], [http://allanmccollum.net/allanmcnyc/Liam_Gillick.html "Allan McCollum at the Serpentine"], ''[[Artscribe]]'', Summer 1989</ref> [[Anish Kapoor]], [[Christian Boltanski]], [[Philippe Parreno]], [[Richard Prince]], [[Wolfgang Tillmans]], [[Gerhard Richter]], [[Gustav Metzger]], [[Damien Hirst]], [[Maria Lassnig]], [[Adrian Berg]], [[Jeff Koons]] and [[Marina Abramović]]. On the ground at the gallery's entrance is a permanent work made by [[Ian Hamilton Finlay]] in collaboration with Peter Coates, and dedicated to [[Diana, Princess of Wales]], the gallery's former patron.

==Serpentine North==
{{main|Serpentine North}}
[[File:Serpentine Sackler Gallery.jpg|200px|thumbnail|right|Serpentine North Gallery]]
In 2013, [[Serpentine North]] was opened to the public named as the Serpentine Sackler Gallery, a name changed to Serpentine North in 2021.<ref>{{cite web |last1=da Silva |first1=José |title=London's Serpentine Galleries finally removes Sackler name from building, replacing it with North |url=https://www.theartnewspaper.com/2022/01/12/serpentine-removes-sackler-name-from-building-replacing-it-with-north |website=The Art Newspaper |date=12 January 2022 |access-date=10 March 2023}}</ref> This gave new life to The Magazine, a [[listed building|Grade II* listed]] former gunpowder store built in 1805,<ref name=EnglishHeritage02>{{National Heritage List for England |num= 1278154|desc= The Magazine |access-date=28 September 2014}}</ref> with the addition of an extension designed by [[Zaha Hadid Architects]]. Located five minutes' walk from Serpentine South across the Serpentine Bridge, it comprises {{convert|900|sqm}} of gallery space, restaurant, shop and social space. The Magazine Restaurant adjoins the gallery space.

[[File:Marina Abramović (London 2014).jpg|thumb|[[Marina Abramović]] on "512 Hours" project (2014)]]

==Pavilions==
Every year since 2000, Serpentine has commissioned a temporary summer [[pavilion]] by a leading architect. The series presents the work of an international architect or design team who has not completed a building in England at the time of the Gallery's invitation. Each Pavilion is completed within six months and is situated on the Serpentine South's lawn for three months for the public to explore.
* 2000: [[Zaha Hadid]]
* 2001: [[Daniel Libeskind]]
* 2002: [[Toyo Ito]]<ref>{{cite news|author=Jonathan Glancey |url=https://www.theguardian.com/culture/2002/jul/08/artsfeatures |title=Now you see it: Toyo Ito's pavilion in Hyde Park |work=The Guardian |date=8 July 2002 |access-date=16 December 2013 |location=London}}</ref>
* 2003: [[Oscar Niemeyer]]<ref>{{cite news|author=Jonathan Glancey |url=https://www.theguardian.com/artanddesign/2003/jun/23/architecture.artsfeatures |title=Oscar Niemeyer's Serpentine pavilion |work=The Guardian |date= 25 June 2003|access-date=16 December 2013 |location=London}}</ref>
* 2005: [[Álvaro Siza]] and [[Eduardo Souto de Moura]]<ref>{{cite web |author=ludwig abache & Carolin Hinne |url=http://www.0lll.com/archgallery2/siza_serpentine/index.htm |title=Eduardo Souto de Moura-Álvaro Siza pavilion |publisher=0lll |access-date=16 December 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131027131435/http://www.0lll.com/archgallery2/siza_serpentine/index.htm |archive-date=27 October 2013 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>
